items: General-purpose, compute-optimized, memory-optimized and storage-optimized instance families fit different bottlenecks. Measure CPU, memory, local I/O and networking rather than defaulting to the largest instance.

EC2 provides guest-OS control. Lambda runs suitable function workloads without server management. ECS and EKS orchestrate containers; Fargate supplies serverless compute for supported ECS/EKS workloads. These are different layers, not interchangeable product names.
Auto Scaling maintains/adjusts capacity; a load balancer distributes requests. Deployment across AZs and externalized session state are separate availability decisions.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A database cache has high memory pressure but low CPU utilization. It must continue running on EC2. Which first change should be evaluated? Choose A memory-optimized instance family sized from measurements. The stated bottleneck is memory. Compute or local-storage optimization alone does not address it. Purchase model and interruption tolerance are separate from resource-family suitability.
Transfer exercise: Match a batch CPU job, memory cache, disposable local scratch job and event-triggered function to a resource model. Explain when scaling and load balancing are both necessary.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/cloud-practitioner-02/cloud-practitioner-02-domain3.html

items: RDS/Aurora fit relational workloads; DynamoDB provides key-value/document access patterns; ElastiCache supplies in-memory caching; Redshift is a data warehouse. These are workload models, not a ranking of universally better databases.

An EC2-hosted database gives more OS/database administration control and more responsibility. Managed databases reduce selected maintenance tasks but still require access, backup, recovery, network and engine choices.

DMS supports supported database migration/replication with cutover planning. Heterogeneous migrations can require schema conversion and application changes; moving rows does not prove all procedures, types and queries are compatible.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A business moves an application to a different managed relational engine. It needs existing data and compatible schema/application behavior. What should be planned? Choose Assess schema/application compatibility and use supported migration/replication tools with validation. Schema conversion, application compatibility and validation remain necessary during heterogeneous migration. DMS data movement is not a guarantee that all engine features migrate unchanged. A cache and DNS data do not replace the relational workload.

Transfer exercise: Compare managed relational, EC2-hosted relational, NoSQL and warehouse requirements. Plan a migration test with row counts, integrity checks, application queries and a rollback window.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/cloud-practitioner-02/cloud-practitioner-02-domain3.html

items: VPC routes select next hops; security groups and NACLs filter traffic at different scopes. Stateful security groups track return traffic; stateless NACL rules require the appropriate return path.

Direct Connect is dedicated private connectivity, not default end-to-end encryption. Site-to-Site VPN supplies IPsec tunneling. PrivateLink exposes supported services privately; Transit Gateway provides hub routing; peering directly connects compatible VPCs without transitive routing.

Route 53 supplies DNS and routing policies. CloudFront supplies content delivery/caching; Global Accelerator improves paths to supported regional TCP/UDP endpoints. Match content distribution versus network acceleration requirements.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A company wants a private dedicated link to AWS and also requires encryption in transit. Which statement is correct? Choose Evaluate Direct Connect plus a supported encryption design such as VPN or eligible MACsec, as required. Dedicated/private transport and encryption are different properties. Direct Connect does not encrypt by default; an appropriate VPN/MACsec/application design must meet the actual scope. DNS and NAT do not supply the required physical circuit.
Transfer exercise: Trace a DNS lookup, content download and private EC2 outbound request. Identify routing, addressing, filtering and encryption separately for each path.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/cloud-practitioner-02/cloud-practitioner-02-domain3.html

items: S3 is object storage, EBS is persistent block storage in an AZ, instance store is ephemeral, and EFS/FSx provide file-system options. Select access model, sharing, persistence, latency and availability before price.

S3 Standard suits frequent access; Standard-IA and One Zone-IA introduce access/minimum-duration and resilience considerations. Glacier Instant Retrieval, Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive have different access/retrieval characteristics. Intelligent-Tiering monitors eligible access patterns; optional archive tiers change retrieval behavior.

Lifecycle can transition or expire eligible objects by date/age; versioning, replication and AWS Backup serve different recovery needs. A transition policy is not an immutable-retention control, and a replica is not proof of a tested restore.

blocks.text: Worked decision: An archive can tolerate long retrieval times and is rarely accessed, but must remain recoverable for years. What must be checked before choosing the cheapest S3 archival class? Choose Retrieval time/cost, minimum-duration charges, resilience and retention requirements. Storage price alone omits retrieval delay and charges, retention and resilience requirements. Bucket naming and unrelated EC2 sizing do not remove archival retrieval behavior.

Transfer exercise: Compare classes for hot assets, infrequently read documents and a long-term archive. State whether each needs immediate retrieval, AZ resilience, version recovery or enforced retention.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/cloud-practitioner-02/cloud-practitioner-02-domain3.html

items: SageMaker AI supports building/training/deploying models; Lex builds conversational interfaces. A managed service does not eliminate data-quality, permissions, evaluation and governance decisions.

Athena runs SQL over data such as S3 datasets; Kinesis Data Streams supports streaming records consumed by applications; Firehose handles managed delivery; Glue integrates/transforms/catalogs data; QuickSight provides BI dashboards.

Choose by the work: conversational intent, model training, ad hoc query, streaming processing, managed delivery, transformation or visualization. A multi-service pipeline may use several of these capabilities.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A team has CSV data in S3, wants occasional SQL analysis and then business dashboards. It does not need model training. Which pair is most appropriate? Choose Athena for SQL and QuickSight for BI visualization. Athena and QuickSight match analysis and visualization. Lex/SageMaker AI address conversational/model workloads, while keys, DNS, queues and block storage are not the requested query/dashboard engines.

Transfer exercise: Design a telemetry-to-dashboard pipeline. Identify which component ingests, transforms, stores, queries and visualizes data; then explain when a custom streaming consumer is needed instead of managed delivery.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/cloud-practitioner-02/cloud-practitioner-02-domain3.html

sections.title: 3.8 — Recognize the service categories beyond core infrastructure

items: Integration: SQS queues work, SNS publishes to subscribers, EventBridge routes events, and Step Functions coordinates workflows. Select delivery and coordination behavior rather than matching the word event alone.

Business applications include Connect for contact centers and SES for email. Developer tools include CodeBuild for builds, CodePipeline for delivery orchestration and X-Ray for distributed tracing. End-user computing includes AppStream, WorkSpaces and WorkSpaces Secure Browser with different delivery models.

Amplify supports frontend/mobile application development; IoT Core supports connecting/managing interactions with IoT devices. AWS Support is customer enablement. Verify current availability and the actual service capability before selecting a product merely by category.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A project needs an application build stage, a deployment pipeline and visibility into requests across services. Which combination fits? Choose CodeBuild, CodePipeline and X-Ray. Build, delivery orchestration and tracing map to CodeBuild, CodePipeline and X-Ray. The alternatives address desktop/email/DNS, queue/storage/reports or contact-center/security/network needs.

Transfer exercise: Match a contact center, transactional email, streamed desktop app, managed desktop, browser-only workspace, mobile frontend and IoT sensor connection to the relevant service category.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/cloud-practitioner-02/cloud-practitioner-02-domain3.html

title: CLF-C02 Domain 4 — Billing, Pricing, and Support
summary: Pricing models, cost tools, Organizations billing, support plans, and AWS technical resources for the 12% billing and support domain.

rows: Savings Plans or eligible Reserved pricing
Reserve capacity in an Availability Zone

blocks.text: AWS Organizations can centralize account management and consolidated billing. Cost allocation and account structure help separate ownership while centralizing financial visibility.

items: Use official AWS documentation, whitepapers, Prescriptive Guidance, Knowledge Center, re:Post, and support resources based on the need.
Support-plan questions test which level of guidance and response is appropriate; avoid memorizing old plan details without checking the current AWS Support page.
AWS Partner Network includes partners that provide software and professional services around AWS.

On-Demand avoids a long-term commitment. Savings Plans commit an eligible hourly spend for a term; Reserved Instance discounts have scope/attribute rules. A regional RI discount does not itself reserve capacity in a selected AZ; capacity reservation is a separate requirement.

Spot fits interruption-tolerant work and spare capacity; Dedicated Hosts address eligible physical-host/tenancy needs. Compare total cost and restart overhead instead of assuming any model always wins.

Review RI flexibility and eligible consolidated-billing discount sharing within Organizations. Data transfer into/out of services, across AZs/Regions and to users has service-specific rules. Storage pricing includes requests, retrieval, minimum durations and transitions as well as stored GB.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A team buys a regional RI discount and then assumes a particular AZ is guaranteed to have capacity at launch time. What is the problem? Choose A regional discount and an AZ capacity reservation are different commitments. Discount eligibility does not guarantee zonal capacity. Review the particular RI scope and a suitable capacity-reservation design when launch availability matters. Savings Plans do not reserve unlimited capacity, and Spot remains interruptible.

Transfer exercise: Compare a commitment discount, a capacity reservation and dedicated tenancy for the same workload. Add transfer and archive-retrieval costs to show why hourly compute price is not the whole estimate.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/cloud-practitioner-02/cloud-practitioner-02-domain4.html

items: Pricing Calculator estimates a planned design from assumptions. Cost Explorer analyzes costs/usage and supports forecasts; detailed billing exports support more granular analysis. None of these validates a bad architecture assumption automatically.

Budgets can alert on actual/forecast amounts and utilization/coverage; notifications and billing data have delay. A budget is not an instantaneous spending cap. Any budget action requires separate supported configuration and permissions.

Organizations provides consolidated billing. Apply and activate eligible cost-allocation tag keys for billing analysis; merely attaching a tag does not guarantee its immediate appearance in reports. Account boundaries and allocation rules determine financial ownership.

blocks.text: Worked decision: Resources are tagged Project=Website, but finance cannot group their costs by that key. What should be checked first? Choose Whether the user-defined tag key is activated for cost allocation and billing data has become available. User-defined cost allocation tags need activation and time to appear in billing data. Network rules, CloudTrail and larger instances do not activate billing dimensions.

Transfer exercise: Build a paper estimate, define actual/forecast budget alerts and describe the notification test. Activate a cost tag in a permitted training account or explain the workflow without creating paid resources.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/cloud-practitioner-02/cloud-practitioner-02-domain4.html

items: Current AWS documentation lists Basic Support and paid offerings including Business Support+, Enterprise Support and Unified Operations. Compare current technical-support scope, response targets and designated guidance rather than memorizing retired plan names or treating response targets as resolution guarantees.

Use documentation, re:Post/Knowledge Center and Prescriptive Guidance for self-service knowledge. Support Center handles support cases; support entitlements determine the available channel and technical response. Trusted Advisor and AWS Health/Health API expose different recommendation and health signals.

AWS Partners include software vendors and integrators; Marketplace distributes third-party products and purchasing entitlements. Professional Services and solutions architects address different assistance needs. Report suspected AWS-resource abuse through the appropriate Trust and Safety process, rather than sending it to an unrelated billing alert.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A team needs information about an AWS event affecting its account resources, rather than a general architecture recommendation. Which resource should it check? Choose AWS Health and the relevant Health API/dashboard information. AWS Health provides relevant health/event information; Trusted Advisor recommendations and cost estimation serve different purposes. Marketplace and infrastructure templates do not replace the event/health signal.

Transfer exercise: Compare current support offerings using the official plan table, record the checked date, and distinguish first-response targets from guaranteed resolution. Identify the right channel for a bill question, an outage and suspected abuse.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/cloud-practitioner-02/cloud-practitioner-02-domain4.html

title: SAA Core Services — Compute and Scaling
summary: EC2 instance design, pricing, storage attachment, Auto Scaling, load balancing, containers, Lambda, and Systems Manager.

items: Choose instance families from workload characteristics rather than memorizing every SKU.
EBS-backed instances keep persistent block data independently of instance lifecycle when configured appropriately; instance store is ephemeral host-attached storage.
Placement groups influence how EC2 instances are placed for latency, throughput, or failure isolation.
IAM roles are the preferred way for EC2 workloads to receive AWS permissions.

blocks.text: An Auto Scaling group maintains or changes instance capacity; an Elastic Load Balancer distributes traffic to healthy targets. A launch template defines how new instances are created. Target tracking follows a target metric; step scaling reacts in increments; scheduled scaling handles known time patterns.

rows: Short-lived event-driven functions without server management
Serverless compute for supported ECS/EKS containers

blocks.text: Systems Manager provides operational capabilities for managed nodes, including inventory, automation, Run Command, patching, and Session Manager. For remote administration, Session Manager can avoid opening inbound SSH/RDP ports.

title: SAA Core Services — Storage and Data Movement
summary: S3 architecture and classes, EBS/EFS/FSx choices, lifecycle, replication, transfer acceleration, DataSync, Storage Gateway, and Snowball Edge (existing customers only; evaluate current alternatives).

items: S3 is object storage with bucket-level namespace and object keys.
Versioning protects against overwrite/deletion scenarios and is a prerequisite for some replication patterns.

Choose storage classes using access and retention requirements, then configure S3 Lifecycle by dates/object age or noncurrent-version age. Lifecycle is not a last-access trigger; Intelligent-Tiering monitors access to move eligible objects among access tiers.
Storage class choice depends on access frequency, retrieval-time tolerance, and minimum storage/retrieval charges.
Presigned URLs provide temporary access without public bucket permissions.

rows: Shared POSIX file system across Linux instances
Online accelerated transfer between storage systems
Hybrid on-premises access to AWS storage
Snowball Edge (existing customers only; evaluate current alternatives)
Faster S3 uploads over long geographic distance

blocks.text: Durability is about retaining data; availability is about being able to access it when needed. Cross-Region replication can satisfy geographic copy or compliance patterns; Multi-AZ service designs protect against an AZ failure without necessarily creating a second Region.

title: SAA Core Services — VPC and Connectivity
summary: CIDR, subnets, routing, security groups/NACLs, NAT, PrivateLink, peering, Transit Gateway, VPN, Direct Connect, and network performance.

items: A subnet is associated with one Availability Zone.
A route table determines next hops; a public subnet has a route to an internet gateway for internet-bound traffic.
An instance also needs an appropriate public IPv4/EIP or IPv6 path and security rules to communicate with the internet.
Private-subnet outbound IPv4 internet access commonly uses a NAT gateway placed in a public subnet.

rows: Return path must be allowed explicitly
Private service exposure without broad routing

blocks.text: Enhanced networking and Elastic Fabric Adapter target high-throughput/low-latency workloads. Global Accelerator improves network path to regional endpoints; CloudFront caches content at edge locations. Choose based on whether the requirement is application content caching or network acceleration.

title: SAA Core Services — Databases and Caching
summary: RDS/Aurora HA and scaling, DynamoDB capacity and indexes, ElastiCache, Redshift, backup, recovery, and database migration.

items: RDS manages supported relational engines; Aurora is AWS-built and compatible with MySQL/PostgreSQL ecosystems.

A single-standby RDS Multi-AZ DB instance provides synchronous standby/failover, and its standby cannot serve reads. A Multi-AZ DB cluster has two readable standbys; Aurora replicas can also serve reads and be failover candidates.
Read replicas are primarily for read scaling and can also support certain DR/reporting patterns.
RDS Proxy pools connections and can improve application resilience around connection storms.
Automated backups and snapshots serve different retention and recovery workflows.
Partition-key design determines distribution and access efficiency.
On-demand capacity fits unpredictable traffic; provisioned capacity fits workloads where capacity can be planned and tuned.
Global secondary indexes provide alternate query keys; global tables replicate across Regions.
DAX is an in-memory DynamoDB-compatible cache. Its microsecond benefit applies to eventually consistent cache hits; strong reads pass through to DynamoDB, and cache misses/expiry still matter.

blocks.text: AWS Database Migration Service supports database migration with minimal downtime patterns; schema-conversion needs depend on whether source and target engines are homogeneous or heterogeneous.

title: SAA Core Services — IAM, Encryption, and Observability
summary: IAM policy evaluation, roles/STS, KMS/Secrets Manager, organizations, CloudTrail, CloudWatch, Config, EventBridge, and operational visibility.

items: Prefer roles and temporary credentials over long-lived access keys for workloads.
Identity-based policies attach to principals; resource-based policies attach to resources that support them.
An explicit deny overrides an allow.

A permissions boundary limits identity-policy grants and grants to a role ARN; it does not grant access. Same-account direct resource-policy grants to an IAM user ARN or assumed-role session ARN have implicit-deny exceptions. Applicable explicit denies still override allows.
Cross-account access commonly combines a trusted role/resource policy with the caller's permission to assume or use it.

rows: Public/private certificates for supported AWS integrations
What is the workload doing? metrics/logs/alarms
How was this resource configured and did it meet a rule?

blocks.text: EventBridge routes events to targets using rules and is useful for event-driven automation. CloudWatch alarms react to metrics. CloudTrail records API events. These may participate in one workflow but are not interchangeable.

title: SAA Core Services — Route 53, CloudFront, and Data Pipelines
summary: Route 53 policies and health checks, CloudFront, SQS/SNS/EventBridge, Kinesis, ingestion, transformation, and analytics services.

rows: Select DNS answers probabilistically by relative weights; caching prevents exact request splits
Send users to the lowest-latency selected Region
Route based on user geographic location
Route by resource/user geography with optional bias
Return multiple records with health preference; all-unhealthy fallback can return unhealthy records

blocks.text: CloudFront caches content at edge locations to reduce latency and origin load. Origins can include S3 and HTTP endpoints. Use signed URLs/cookies and origin access controls when private content or private S3 origins are required.

items: Kinesis Data Streams handles real-time streaming records with consumer applications.
Amazon Data Firehose delivers streaming data to supported destinations with managed delivery.
AWS Glue provides data integration and ETL capabilities.
Athena queries data in S3 with SQL.
Lake Formation helps build and govern data lakes.

title: SAA Domain 1 — Design Secure Architectures
summary: Secure access, workload protection, network boundaries, encryption, and data controls for the 30% Secure Architectures domain.

items: Prefer federated workforce access and roles over creating unnecessary long-lived IAM users.
Use temporary credentials for applications, automation, and cross-account access.
Apply least privilege and use explicit denies or service-control guardrails where the requirement calls for centralized restrictions.
Use resource policies where supported to grant controlled cross-account or service access.

Permissions boundaries do not grant permissions. Apply the identity-policy intersection model, then evaluate direct resource-policy grants by principal type; a same-account grant to a user ARN or role-session ARN can bypass an implicit boundary deny, but not an applicable explicit deny.

rows: Private AWS service access from a VPC

items: Encrypt data at rest with service-supported KMS integration when key governance is required.
Use TLS for data in transit.
Secrets Manager is for secrets such as database credentials; KMS is for cryptographic keys.
S3 Block Public Access, bucket policies, access points, and object ownership settings should reflect the intended access model.
Classify sensitive data and use Macie where S3 sensitive-data discovery is required.

blocks.text: CloudTrail records API activity, Config evaluates configuration state, CloudWatch provides metrics/logs/alarms, Security Hub aggregates security findings, and centralized logging supports investigation. The exam often asks which control is preventive, detective, or corrective.

items: Identify the principal (human, role or role session), action, resource, account boundary and conditions before evaluating policy. Federate workforce access where appropriate; use roles/STS for temporary workload credentials.

An identity-policy allow is not sufficient when an applicable explicit deny, SCP, boundary or session constraint prevents it. Boundaries/SCPs do not grant access. Direct same-account user/session resource grants have documented implicit-deny exceptions; key policies and service rules still matter.

For cross-account role use, the target role trust permits the source principal, the caller has sts:AssumeRole permission and the assumed role has required resource permissions. Control Tower and Organizations provide multi-account governance; choose the least privilege that matches the workload.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A workload in Account A must read a bucket in B with temporary credentials. The role in B has s3:GetObject permissions but no trust for A. What is missing? Choose An appropriate trust relationship plus caller sts:AssumeRole permission. Role resource permissions describe what the assumed role can do; trust/caller permissions allow assumption. Public access violates the intended restricted design. Boundaries and SCPs do not grant role trust or resource access.

Transfer exercise: Trace caller identity, trust policy, assumed session, role permissions, bucket policy and any KMS key policy. Add an explicit deny and explain its effect; then distinguish a role ARN grant from a session ARN grant.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/solutions-architect-associate-03/solutions-architect-associate-03-domain1.html

sections.title: 1.2 — Secure the request path and application identity

items: Separate public entry points, private application tiers and data stores. Security groups permit required resource flows; NACLs evaluate ordered stateless subnet rules including return traffic. A private subnet name or missing public IPv4 is not proof of isolation for every address family.

Use supported endpoints for private service access, selecting gateway versus interface endpoints deliberately. Endpoint policies, IAM and resource policies work together. Direct Connect is not default encryption; VPN/TLS/MACsec requirements must be evaluated separately.

WAF filters supported HTTP/S attacks, Shield addresses DDoS, GuardDuty detects threats, Inspector assesses vulnerabilities and Cognito can provide application user identity. These controls solve separate problems; workload credentials belong in suitable role/secret mechanisms.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A private application needs frequent S3 access without NAT processing. Its users still require application authentication. Which design addresses both without conflating them? Choose An S3 gateway endpoint with appropriate policies, plus an application identity/authentication design. A gateway endpoint changes the S3 network path; it does not authenticate application users or grant all data access. IAM/resource policies and user identity remain separate. Public buckets and unencrypted-private assumptions do not meet the stated design.

Transfer exercise: Draw a complete client-to-database path, labeling TLS termination, user authentication, service role, endpoint access and network rules. Explain why a threat-detection finding is not a preventive access policy.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/solutions-architect-associate-03/solutions-architect-associate-03-domain1.html

items: KMS key policies, IAM permissions and encryption context/conditions determine key use; encrypting data does not neutralize an overly broad read permission. Plan key rotation/lifecycle and certificate renewal; ACM TLS certificates serve a different role from application secrets.

S3 Block Public Access, ownership and resource policies restrict access. A presigned URL is transferable bearer access within the signing principal permissions and credential lifetime, not recipient-bound identity. Use a separate authentication/control design if sharing must be nontransferable.

Versioning preserves previous versions; replication needs both buckets versioned, permission/encryption setup and status validation. Existing objects need a backfill strategy. Backup, deletion recovery and Object Lock retention are distinct requirements; test recovery with the intended permissions.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A compliance requirement says archived objects must not be deletable before their retention date, even by ordinary administrators. Which design should be evaluated? Choose Appropriate S3 Object Lock retention configuration and controlled administration, with backup/restore validation. Object Lock provides retention controls suited to the specified mode/permissions. Lifecycle schedules storage actions, replication makes copies and presigned URLs authorize requests; none alone guarantees immutable retention. Evaluate governance versus compliance mode and the applicable legal requirements.

Transfer exercise: Build a source/destination retention-and-access matrix: writer, reader, replicator, key administrator and recovery operator. Test overwrite, ordinary delete, explicit version delete and restore in a permitted disposable environment.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/solutions-architect-associate-03/solutions-architect-associate-03-domain1.html

title: SAA Domain 2 — Design Resilient Architectures
summary: Loose coupling, multi-AZ design, backups, queues, health checks, failover, and disaster-recovery patterns for the 26% Resilient Architectures domain.

items: Use SQS to buffer work between producers and consumers and absorb traffic bursts.
Use SNS when one event must fan out to multiple subscribers.
Use EventBridge for event routing across sources and targets.
Keep application tiers stateless where possible so instances can be replaced or scaled horizontally.
Use managed services and asynchronous workflows to reduce dependencies between components.

rows: Auto Scaling group with multiple instances
Health checks and failover routing/load balancing
Multi-Region DR pattern appropriate to RTO/RPO

blocks.text: Choose a recovery design from business RTO and RPO. Backups generally cost less but recover more slowly; warm standby or active/active designs cost more but can recover faster. Replication improves recovery options but does not replace backup or protection against logical corruption.

rows: Lowest steady cost, highest recovery time
Core services kept ready; scale during recovery
Fastest failover, highest cost and complexity

sections.title: Design for failure and service limits

blocks.text: Architectures should anticipate service quotas, retry transient failures with appropriate backoff, use idempotent operations where possible, and avoid retry storms. Health checks must measure the user-facing dependency that actually determines availability.

sections.title: 2.1 — Loose coupling with correct failure semantics

items: Use queues to absorb bursts and separate producer/worker scaling. SQS standard queues are at-least-once with best-effort ordering; processing must be idempotent. Visibility hides in-flight work temporarily, and successful processing must be acknowledged/deleted.

SNS fans out to subscribers; EventBridge routes events; Step Functions orchestrates stateful workflows; API Gateway supplies managed API entry capabilities. Choose synchronous response, queue, event bus or orchestration from required behavior, not a shared event keyword.

Stateful sessions/files on one instance prevent easy horizontal replacement. Externalize appropriate state, choose container/serverless services based on runtime/operational constraints, and scale workers against backlog and processing time rather than an unrelated metric.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A worker commits an order side effect but crashes before deleting its SQS message. The order must not be charged twice after retry. What is required? Choose An idempotency key or equivalent durable deduplication around the side effect. At-least-once delivery and crash windows require application idempotency. Visibility can reduce concurrent processing but is not exactly-once protection. Queue access and ALB health do not atomically deduplicate the business operation.

Transfer exercise: Walk through publish, receive, visibility expiry, side effect, acknowledgement and DLQ redrive. Inject failure before and after the side effect and identify which durable record prevents duplicate business effects.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/solutions-architect-associate-03/solutions-architect-associate-03-domain2.html

sections.title: 2.2 — Failure domains, health and recovery evidence

items: Deploy independent serving capacity across AZs, configure load-balancer target health and ASG ELB health checks where application failures should cause replacement, and maintain enough surviving capacity. ALB can fail open when all targets are unhealthy; a health check is not a universal safety barrier.

Single-standby RDS Multi-AZ, readable Multi-AZ clusters and Aurora replicas have different read/failover mechanics. Match recovery behavior, client reconnects, replication and backup to the database deployment rather than using one standby slogan.

Choose DR from measured RTO/RPO and test data recovery, dependencies, credentials, quotas, routing and startup order. Backup/restore, pilot light, warm standby and active/active have relative cost/recovery tradeoffs, not universal minute guarantees. Workload metrics, logs and traces supply evidence of recovery.

blocks.text: Worked decision: An ALB detects unhealthy application targets, but their EC2 status checks pass and the ASG never replaces them. What configuration should be reviewed? Choose ASG Elastic Load Balancing health-check integration and grace-period behavior. Target-group application checks and ASG replacement checks are separate. Enable the appropriate ELB health checks and grace period, and verify replacement behavior. Storage lifecycle, database replicas and audit logging do not establish that integration.

Transfer exercise: Test instance loss, application-only failure, AZ loss and all-target failure separately. Record recovery time and validate the data recovery point, then compare both against the business targets.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/solutions-architect-associate-03/solutions-architect-associate-03-domain2.html

title: SAA Domain 3 — Design High-Performing Architectures
summary: Choose performant storage, compute, database, network, caching, and data-ingestion architectures for the 24% High-Performing domain.

rows: Appropriate EBS volume type and provisioned performance
EFS with performance/throughput mode matched to workload

items: Choose instance families based on compute, memory, storage, accelerator, and network requirements.
Use Auto Scaling to match capacity to load and load balancers to distribute requests.
Use Lambda for suitable event-driven workloads where scaling without server management is valuable.
Use placement groups, enhanced networking, or EFA for specialized low-latency/high-throughput EC2 workloads.
Use read replicas for relational read scaling and caching for repeated hot reads.
Choose DynamoDB keys that distribute traffic and satisfy access patterns; add indexes deliberately.
DAX can reduce DynamoDB read latency for cacheable workloads.
Aurora read replicas and reader endpoints can scale reads for compatible relational workloads.

rows: Cache static/dynamic content close to users
Improve global network path to regional endpoints
Real-time streaming records with custom consumers
Cache with CloudFront, ElastiCache, DAX, or application cache as appropriate

items: EBS provides persistent AZ-scoped block volumes; volume type and provisioned IOPS/throughput must match the instance and workload. A volume remaining after stop differs from DeleteOnTermination behavior. Instance store is scratch storage that can be lost on stop/termination or host loss.

EFS provides shared Linux/POSIX-style access; choose Regional versus One Zone, throughput and performance options against requirements. FSx alternatives target Windows, Lustre, ONTAP or OpenZFS workloads; a shared-file requirement does not automatically fit a block volume.

S3 handles objects with key-based access; multipart/parallel access, object size and request patterns affect performance. DataSync and hybrid gateways solve movement/interface needs rather than making every storage service interchangeable. Measure IOPS, throughput, latency and concurrency separately.

blocks.text: Worked decision: Two application servers in different AZs need simultaneous access to the same Linux file tree. They cannot be changed to use an object API. Which initial design is most appropriate? Choose A Regional EFS file system with suitable mount targets and throughput settings. Regional EFS fits shared cross-AZ Linux file access. EBS attachments are AZ-scoped, instance stores do not synchronize automatically and object interfaces are not identical to POSIX file semantics.

Transfer exercise: For a small-I/O database and a large sequential file workload, separate required IOPS from MB/s. Check instance limits as well as storage limits and compare persistent, shared and disposable storage choices.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/solutions-architect-associate-03/solutions-architect-associate-03-domain3.html

sections.title: 3.2 — Choose and scale compute for the bottleneck

items: Match EC2 family/size to CPU, memory, storage, network and accelerator demand. Horizontal scaling needs a partitionable/stateless design; vertical scaling changes one node and retains its failure boundary. Benchmark before assuming the largest size is efficient.

Target tracking needs a metric that changes proportionally with capacity, such as a suitable average utilization or request metric. Step and scheduled scaling fit different triggers. For queues, consider backlog per worker and processing duration; also plan warmup, scale-in and service quotas.

For Lambda, consider memory/CPU coupling, concurrency, execution limits and downstream connection pressure. ECS/EKS orchestrate containers; Fargate supplies supported serverless task compute. Batch/EMR target suitable batch/distributed processing. Placement/EFA choices have supported-instance and topology constraints.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A worker fleet is CPU-idle while processing a growing backlog of slow external API calls. Which scaling signal best reflects the business bottleneck? Choose A suitable backlog-per-worker/processing-time metric, with downstream rate limits considered. Backlog and processing time capture unmet work even when the process waits on I/O. Scaling must respect downstream capacity and rate limits. CPU alone can remain low; identity count and bucket age do not measure work demand.
Transfer exercise: Choose metrics and scale limits for CPU-bound, I/O-bound and scheduled workloads. Explain how adding workers can worsen throttling if a downstream API is already saturated.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/solutions-architect-associate-03/solutions-architect-associate-03-domain3.html

sections.title: 3.3 — Database access patterns, consistency and connections

items: Relational replicas offload suitable reads but may lag. RDS Proxy pools supported connections; reader endpoints distribute connections rather than guaranteeing equal query cost. Distinguish single-standby Multi-AZ, readable Multi-AZ clusters and Aurora read/failover roles.

DynamoDB partition keys must spread load and support access patterns. GSIs add alternate keys and use eventually consistent reads; LSIs have creation/key constraints. Strong and eventual reads and write item sizes consume capacity differently; round per-request size requirements before estimating provisioned demand.

On-demand adapts capacity but retains warm-throughput/partition/table limits. DAX accelerates eventual cache hits, not strongly consistent reads. ElastiCache reduces repeated work where freshness requirements permit. Database-engine and migration choices require schema, transaction, query and compatibility analysis.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A user must immediately read a just-written DynamoDB value with a strong consistency requirement. Which design avoids relying on stale cached data? Choose A supported strongly consistent table read rather than assuming a DAX cache hit is strongly consistent. Use a supported strong read for that requirement. DAX eventual caches and GSIs do not guarantee the same freshness, and asynchronously replicated paths may lag. A fast response is not a consistency guarantee.

sections.title: 3.4 — Network topology, transport and DNS behavior

items: Plan nonoverlapping address ranges, AZ subnets and route tables, including return paths and IPv4/IPv6 differences. Select gateway/interface endpoints, PrivateLink, peering or Transit Gateway from service exposure versus network-routing requirements.

ALB serves HTTP-layer routing; NLB serves TCP/UDP/TLS connection requirements; GWLB supports appropriate virtual network-appliance insertion. CloudFront caches/delivers HTTP content, while Global Accelerator supplies static anycast entry and AWS-network routing to supported endpoints.

Route 53 weighted routing selects DNS responses probabilistically, with caching effects; latency routing uses AWS latency information, not simply map distance. Multivalue can return up to eight records and depends on health-check configuration, including an all-unhealthy fallback. DNS TTL limits how quickly clients observe failover.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A global UDP application requires static anycast entry addresses and routing to healthy regional endpoints. It does not use HTTP content caching. Which option fits? Choose Global Accelerator with supported regional endpoints. Global Accelerator addresses supported TCP/UDP application entry and network paths. CloudFront and S3 Transfer Acceleration are not generic UDP proxies; DNS geolocation selects answers rather than providing the stated accelerator capability.

Transfer exercise: Compare a public HTTP site, UDP game endpoint and security-appliance path. Include addressing, health, routing, TLS/transport and DNS caching in the decision rather than choosing by service familiarity.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/solutions-architect-associate-03/solutions-architect-associate-03-domain3.html

items: Kinesis Data Streams supports streaming records consumed by applications; ordering is scoped to shard/partition-key sequencing, with producer retry and consumer checkpoint behavior to design. Firehose supplies managed buffered delivery and optional transformations to supported destinations.

Use Glue for suitable integration, transformation and catalog work; EMR for appropriate distributed processing; Athena for queries and BI tools for visualization. Partitioned/columnar formats can reduce scanned data, but conversion and partition strategy must preserve schema and query requirements.

DataSync, Storage Gateway and supported transfer services address different movement and interface needs. Secure ingestion endpoints, roles, encryption, data-lake access and catalog governance. Design throughput, buffering, latency, replay and malformed-record handling together.

blocks.text: Worked decision: Sensors require custom per-device stream processing and replay, followed by analytics in S3. Which design best preserves the processing requirement? Choose Kinesis Data Streams with device partition keys and checkpointed consumers, followed by suitable S3 delivery/analytics. A stream and consumers provide custom processing/replay within configured retention and per-key ordering design. Managed delivery is useful downstream but does not replace all stream-consumer semantics. Email and overwrites do not satisfy the data pipeline.

Transfer exercise: Sketch ingestion, authentication, buffer, transformation, error path, S3 partitioning, catalog, query and dashboard. Compare .csv and columnar output for a specific query and test replay without duplicate side effects.

items: Match S3 storage class to access frequency, retrieval-time tolerance, object size, and retention period.
Use lifecycle policies to transition or expire data automatically.
Delete unattached EBS volumes and obsolete snapshots according to retention policy.
Use the storage model that meets the requirement instead of defaulting to the highest-performance tier.

rows: Savings Plans or eligible Reserved pricing
Auto Scaling to avoid idle capacity

items: Right-size RDS instances/storage and use suitable purchase models where available.
DynamoDB on-demand can avoid capacity planning for unpredictable workloads; provisioned capacity can be cost-effective when usage is predictable.
Archive infrequently accessed data outside expensive primary database storage when the application permits.
Caching can reduce expensive repeated database work, but only when cache cost and consistency needs make sense.

blocks.text: Data transfer often changes the cheapest architecture. Keep high-volume traffic local to an AZ/Region when requirements allow, use CloudFront to reduce repeated origin transfer for cacheable content, avoid unnecessary NAT gateway paths for AWS-service traffic by using appropriate VPC endpoints, and compare Direct Connect/VPN choices against throughput and business needs.
SAA cost questions frequently hide the cost driver in data transfer or idle capacity rather than in the obvious service price.

items: Compare object/file/block access requirements before cost. Include stored bytes, provisioned performance, requests, transitions, retrieval, minimum-duration/object-size rules, replicas and transfers. The cheapest GB price may violate retrieval or durability requirements.

Choose lifecycle transitions by eligible object/version age and retention needs. Handle noncurrent versions and multipart leftovers deliberately. Intelligent-Tiering monitors eligible access patterns; archive tiers can require restore steps. Requester Pays changes who is billed for supported request/transfer charges, not ownership or authorization.

Size persistent storage and backup retention from recovery/compliance needs. Delete only genuinely unused volumes/snapshots under policy; snapshot dependencies mean billed savings may differ from visible snapshot count. Compare DataSync/transfer/gateway options against scale, bandwidth and change rate.

blocks.text: Worked decision: A team archives small objects and retrieves them frequently. Its storage bill falls but request/retrieval charges rise sharply. What did the design omit? Choose Object size, access frequency, retrieval and minimum-duration/request economics. Storage-class selection requires the full access and lifecycle cost, including small-object and retrieval constraints. Identity-group count does not explain it; archives are not universally instant/free, and block storage is not a blanket fix for an object workload.

Transfer exercise: Write a symbolic monthly cost comparison for hot storage versus an archival tier, including a retrieval event and early deletion. Explain which measurements determine the break-even decision.

sections.title: 4.2 — Commit the baseline and scale the variable work

items: Right-size and measure before choosing commitments. Use eligible Savings Plans/Reserved discounts for a stable baseline; On-Demand for flexibility; Spot for interruption-tolerant work after accounting for capacity/restart behavior. A discount is not a capacity guarantee.

Scale off idle capacity, schedule suitable non-production environments and compare serverless versus containers/VMs for actual runtime, concurrency and operational needs. Lambda is not automatically cheapest at every utilization, and Dedicated Hosts serve tenancy/license requirements rather than universal savings.

Compute topology also determines load-balancing, network and resilience costs. Select ALB/NLB/GWLB and horizontal/vertical/suspend/hibernate choices from protocol, state and availability requirements. Outposts/hybrid choices add operational and placement considerations.

blocks.text: Worked decision: An application has a measured stable baseline plus short seasonal peaks, and cannot tolerate interruption for customer transactions. Which purchase strategy should be evaluated? Choose A suitable baseline commitment with elastic On-Demand capacity for peaks. Commitment on measured baseline plus flexible peak capacity matches predictable and variable demand. Committing to peaks risks unused spend; Spot-only ignores interruption constraints; dedicated tenancy is not a universal cost discount.

Transfer exercise: Separate baseline and peak spend, include load balancer/transfer/operational costs, and compare a scheduled development environment with a continuously required production environment.
Scope reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/solutions-architect-associate-03/solutions-architect-associate-03-domain4.html

items: Choose engine/model from transactions, access patterns, schema, scale and compatibility; compare relational, key-value/document, time-series and analytical workloads deliberately. A low instance rate is not a reason to select an incompatible data model.

For RDS/Aurora evaluate instance/storage right-sizing, appropriate purchase models, replicas, connections and retention. For DynamoDB compare on-demand/provisioned demand economics, key distribution, indexes and cache cost; a cache adds its own operations and consistency requirements.

Backups, cross-Region copies, retention and migrations all cost money but meet different requirements. Heterogeneous migration needs schema/application validation. Estimate the cost of read scaling, data retention and recovery before eliminating safeguards for savings.

blocks.text: Worked decision: An RDS instance averages low CPU, but the team has not measured memory, I/O latency, connections or peak demand. What is the best cost-optimization next step? Choose Measure the full workload and evaluate a smaller suitable configuration against peaks and recovery requirements. Low average CPU is only one signal. Memory, I/O, connections, peaks and resilience constrain safe rightsizing. Removing recovery controls or adding an unvalidated cache can change correctness or availability rather than remove waste.

Transfer exercise: Compare two database configurations using peak demand, storage growth, backup retention and recovery goals. State when an index/cache/replica lowers total work and when it adds unnecessary cost.

sections.title: 4.4 — Network cost follows the traffic path

items: Identify bytes and paths: same-AZ, cross-AZ, cross-Region, service endpoint, NAT, dedicated link and internet delivery. Data-transfer pricing is service-specific; do not assume all same-Region traffic is free or all cross-AZ paths charge identically.

An S3 gateway endpoint can avoid NAT processing for eligible traffic without gateway-endpoint hourly/data fees. Interface endpoints have different charging/availability properties. For zonal NAT compare same-AZ egress per AZ with a shared dependency; regional NAT is a distinct current multi-AZ option.

Compare Direct Connect, VPN and internet designs using bandwidth, encryption, redundancy and business targets. CloudFront may reduce repeated origin work/transfer, but include CDN/request/invalidations and cache hit behavior. Do not minimize transfer by removing required failure isolation.

blocks.text: Worked decision: Private instances send large S3 volumes through a NAT gateway. The workload must keep S3 access private and maintain its AZ-resilience design. What should be evaluated first? Choose S3 gateway endpoints with the relevant subnet route-table associations and access policies. Gateway endpoints can remove eligible S3 traffic from NAT without gateway-endpoint charges. Validate route/policy scope. A single zonal NAT can introduce an AZ dependency, public access changes authorization, and interface endpoint costs are different.

sections.title: Linux client desktops: boot, config files and identity (1.9)

blocks.text: Linux is free, open-source and supported by a community rather than one company. Distributions such as Ubuntu and Red Hat package the same kernel with different tools. At boot, firmware (BIOS or UEFI) hands off to a bootloader, which starts the kernel. The kernel starts systemd, which manages background services called daemons.

rows: User account entries (names, IDs, home folders)
Hashed passwords, readable only by root
Manual name-to-IP mappings, checked before DNS

blocks.text: Linux configuration lives in plain text files under /etc. Know which file holds passwords, which maps names locally, and which lists DNS servers.

rows: Trace the route to a host
Edit a file in a simple editor

items: chmod uses octal numbers: 4 is read, 2 is write, 1 is execute. Add them per owner, group and others. chmod 764 gives the owner rwx, the group rw and others r.
Prefer sudo for a single administrative command. su switches the whole session to the superuser.

blocks.text: Standard users cannot read /etc/shadow. Protecting it is why password hashes are not visible to ordinary accounts.

sections.title: Securing SOHO wireless and wired networks (2.10)

blocks.text: A small office or home router is the heart of the network, and most of the hardening is done in its admin console.

items: Change the default administrator password before anything else. Default logins are public knowledge.
Keep the router firmware updated. Firmware is the router's operating system, and updates carry security patches.
Disable UPnP (Universal Plug and Play). It lets internal apps open firewall ports automatically, which is a serious security risk.
Place internet-facing services such as a web server in a DMZ (demilitarized zone), a screened subnet that visitors can reach but that cannot reach the private network.
Use WPA2 at a minimum and WPA3 when available. Hiding the SSID broadcast is security through obscurity and does not stop a determined attacker.
Create a guest network for visitors and IoT devices so they get internet access without reaching trusted devices.
Disable unused switch ports so an intruder cannot plug in.
Use port forwarding only when a service must be reachable from the internet, because each forward is a permanent opening in the firewall.

blocks.text: The three SOHO essentials on the exam: change the default password, disable UPnP, and use WPA2 or WPA3 with a guest network for untrusted devices.

items: Download the browser from the developer's official site. Verify the installer by comparing its SHA-256 hash with the hash the developer publishes.
Keep the browser patched; modern browsers update automatically, and updates include security fixes.
Install extensions only from official stores. Extensions run with the browser's own access, so a malicious one can read keystrokes, passwords and screen contents.
Use a password manager to create and store a unique password for each site, which stops password reuse from spreading a breach.

blocks.text: A 'connection is not private' warning is a red flag. Causes include an expired certificate, a certificate that does not match the domain name, a certificate signed by an authority the browser does not trust, or a wrong system date and time.

items: Keep the pop-up blocker on and allow exceptions only for trusted sites.
Clear the cache when pages misbehave, since corrupted cached data causes display and login problems.
Private browsing does not save history, cookies or cache on the local machine after the window closes. It does not hide your traffic from the network or the site.
A corporate proxy server filters web traffic. Configure the proxy address and port in the browser when your organization requires it.
Secure DNS (DNS over HTTPS) encrypts DNS queries so local observers cannot see which sites you look up.

blocks.text: A proxy server is a filtering middleman between you and the web. It is not the same as a VPN, which encrypts the whole connection.

items: Sideloading means installing apps from unofficial stores or websites. Malicious apps are often disguised as legitimate ones, a technique called application spoofing.
Rooting (Android) and jailbreaking (iOS) disable the built-in security protections so you get full control. They make malware far easier to run.

Symptoms of mobile malware include a sudden spike in data usage, degraded performance that a restart does not fix, limited or no connectivity, excess ads or adware, fake security warnings, and apps that crash or change settings on their own.
For minor problems such as adware, an anti-malware scan may remove the offending app.

For a serious infection or a suspected data leak, back up essential data, perform a factory reset, restore from a clean backup, then change the passwords for every cloud account that synced to the device and enable multifactor authentication.

blocks.text: The reset-and-rotate sequence is the answer to most mobile infection scenarios: wipe the device, then change passwords and enable MFA.

sections.title: Tools and methods that fight malware (2.4)

items: Safe mode and the recovery environment load only essential files, so many malware types cannot start and can be removed.
Antivirus focuses on viruses; anti-malware covers a broader set such as Trojans, spyware and ransomware. In practice, use both.
Endpoint detection and response (EDR) watches behavior on each device, such as a process trying to access files it should not touch.
Managed detection and response (MDR) outsources 24/7 monitoring to a third party, which suits small and medium businesses without a security operations center.
Extended detection and response (XDR) combines data from endpoints, networks, email and cloud services into one view.
An email security gateway filters spam, phishing and suspicious attachments before they reach inboxes. Email is the most common malware delivery route.
A software firewall decides which traffic gets in and out, and a personal firewall can block malware from contacting its control server.
User education, especially anti-phishing training, is one of the strongest defenses because human error starts many breaches.
Reinstalling the operating system gives a clean state. Back up critical data first.

blocks.text: Social engineering manipulates people instead of technology. Attackers know firewalls are hard to beat, so they target the human who can open the door.

rows: Fake email that asks you to click a link or confirm login details
Phone call from a fake agency or support desk
Fake text message with a malicious link
Malicious QR code posted where people scan it

Watching someone enter a PIN or password
Following an authorized person through a secured door
Pretending to be trusted staff, such as IT support or a delivery driver

items: Denial of service (DoS) floods one system with traffic. A DDoS uses thousands of compromised machines, called a botnet.
An evil twin is a fake Wi-Fi access point that imitates a legitimate network.
An on-path (man-in-the-middle) attack secretly intercepts communication between two parties.
A zero-day attack exploits a vulnerability before a patch exists.
Spoofing pretends to be something else: a fake sender address, a fake IP source or a fake caller ID.
Brute force tries every combination. A dictionary attack tries a list of common passwords.
Insider threats come from employees, while SQL injection and cross-site scripting attack web applications.
A supply-chain attack compromises a trusted vendor to reach its customers, as in the SolarWinds case.

Vulnerabilities are the weak points attackers use: non-compliant systems that break security policy, unpatched systems missing updates, unprotected systems with no antivirus or firewall, and end-of-life systems that no longer receive support.

blocks.text: Tailgating is physical, not technical. Phishing is about the message; tailgating is about the door.

Guarantees a clean state when the infection is too deep

Stops reinfection and closes known gaps

Teach them to recognize phishing and avoid risky downloads

The 3-2-1 backup rule: keep three copies of the data, on two different media types, with one copy offsite. Rotation schemes include on-site versus off-site storage and grandfather-father-son (GFS), which keeps daily, weekly and monthly sets.
A backup you have never restored is a guess. Test restores on a schedule, and record how often you test.

Professional communication is scored in scenarios. Choose the answer that keeps the customer informed, respected and in control of the outcome.
